cases.name: Linda Childers
cases.about: Childers and her late husband were well-known for their restaurant and hardware store. The building was recently turned into a cafe in 2020. "I tell you, they made a huge impact on Fort Calhoun," cafe owner Debbie Schultz said. The owner says Cherry Hill Church & Community Coffee House still serves customers who remember the Childers. "It's been fun to kind of get to know her through them," Schultz said. "There isn't a person that's lived there in the last 50 years that doesn't know her and her husband and her family," Caruso said. "...she was such a beautiful soul. She's a kind person. And she was a pillar of the community. Community. There was no reason for this," said Linda's niece Cindy Childers.
cases.narrative: On 8/14/2023, her stepdaughter found her deceased in her kitchen. Her autopsy determined the cause was homicide, caused by multiple wounds.
